In the Data For Good generative AI white paper, the initial estimated carbon footprint for training the BLOOM model was 30 tonnes CO2eq (based on energy consumption of 433 MWh and carbon intensity of 57 g CO2eq/kWh). When extending the scope to include additional factors such as the consumption of all data center equipment (increasing energy consumption from 433 MWh to 690 MWh), the impact of server and GPU manufacturing (considering a 6-year lifespan and associated CO2eq emissions), and the development phase (including tests, evaluations, and corrections), the total estimated carbon footprint increased significantly.

Specifically, the impact of training alone rose from 39.3 tonnes CO2eq (after including full data center consumption but excluding manufacturing) to 50.5 tonnes CO2eq when including manufacturing impacts. Adding the development phase added an additional 73.32 tonnes CO2eq, resulting in a total full-scope estimate of 123.82 tonnes CO2eq.

Thus, BLOOM's estimated training carbon footprint increased from an initial estimate of about 30 tonnes CO2eq to a full-scope estimate of approximately 124 tonnes CO2eq, which is about four times higher than the initial naive estimate.
